Hi Samantha —

Appreciate the clear questions. Short answers up front, then a recommended contract clause.

1) Streaming: we bill based on the model-side generated tokens (the authoritative token count). For streaming, each token emitted by the model is billable the moment it is generated; we do not double-count retransmissions. Practically this means streaming and non-streaming requests are treated the same for billable-token totals.

2) Rounding: for usage-based billing we currently round at the request level to the nearest whole token, then aggregate daily for metering and monthly for invoicing. So rounding occurs per-request (token fractions from tokenization are rounded per-request), not per-minute.

Recommended clause (for your redline):
- "Billable Tokens" means the number of tokens generated by the model in response to a Customer request. For streaming responses, Billable Tokens are counted at the model emission event level; duplicate or retransmitted frames are excluded. Fractions resulting from tokenization are rounded to the nearest whole token at the per-request level. Daily aggregates of Billable Tokens will be used for usage reporting; monthly invoice quantities will reflect the summed daily aggregates.

I've attached a one-page draft clause (RWD-commit-term-draft.pdf) and annotated the CSV you sent with a few examples.

If that matches, Ben and I can propose how to tie this into the commit tiers (e.g., committing to X monthly billable tokens with tiered discounts and clear overage pricing).

Looping in a pricing note from my side: if Novari wants a commit-based discount schedule, we should be explicit in the SOW about:

- The commit period (monthly vs. annual). We recommend monthly commits with an annual true-up for early-stage customers to avoid lock-in.
- Overage handling: overages billed at the committed-tier per-token rate for the first 10% over, then bumped to list overage rate beyond that (or negotiated).
- Rounding impact: to keep forecasts simple for both parties, suggest we add an example table in the SOW: sample request sizes -> tokenized counts -> billed tokens. That will also make legal comfortable.

Proposed short paragraph to add to the clause Marissa drafted:
- "For purposes of discounting, the Customer's committed quantity will be measured in monthly Billable Tokens as reported in Redwood's usage report. Discounts will apply to the committed quantity. If monthly Billable Tokens exceed the committed quantity, overage charges will apply as set forth in the SOW. All billing calculations are rounded per-request before aggregation as set forth above."

If Novari confirms the per-request rounding approach we're good to lock the pricing terms.
